title: Privacy Shielding, AuthZ Lifecycle, and Compliance Evidence Playbook
author: Leah Nguyen
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines a cross-domain operational approach for: privacy shielding (data minimization and pseudonymization), authorization (AuthZ) lifecycle controls, audit log requirements, data residency & retention enforcement, integration points with Secure SDLC, incident response evidence preservation, and compliance evidence orchestration. It establishes concrete controls, owners, thresholds, and procedural steps to reduce compliance risk while preserving developer velocity.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood production and staging systems that process customer data (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control planes).
- Cross-functional: Security, Infra, Eng Platform, Product, Legal.
- Exempts ephemeral developer sandboxes without production credentials (see Exceptions section).

Definitions:
- Privacy Shielding: techniques that reduce identifiability of personal data (e.g., hashing, tokenization, truncation).
- AuthZ Service: internal authorization gateway and role store (service name: authz-service).
- Audit Pipeline: centralized log ingestion & retention pipeline (services: fluentd -> audit-pipeline -> evidence-bucket).
- Evidence Artifact: packaged logs + metadata required for compliance audits.

Ownership and RACI (high level):
- Security: overall owner of this playbook, compliance evidence validation, exception reviews.
- Infra (logging): responsible for audit-pipeline availability and retention enforcement.
- Eng Platform: integrates AuthZ hooks into runtime and CI.
- Product/Legal: sets retention policy baselines for specific customers/regions.

Data classification and shielding matrix (summary):
| Classification | Example fields | Shielding requirement | Storage tier |
|---------------|----------------|----------------------|--------------|
| PII-high | full name, email, national id | Pseudonymize + access-control via SOD, encrypt with KMS CMK | regional GCS/AWS (customer region) |
| PII-low | account type, usage metrics | Truncate/aggregate, role-based access | cross-region permissible with encryption |
| Non-PII | latency metrics, non-identifying telemetry | None required beyond standard logging | aggregated telemetry store |

(Implementation note: use authz-service labels to gate access to PII-high buckets. Use KMS CMK per-region; key rotation window 90 days.)

AuthZ Lifecycle (provision -> review -> revoke):
1. Provisioning:
  - All roles must be created via the roles-as-code repo (git repo: infra/authz-roles).
  - Role manifests include: role_name, allowed_resources, justification, owner, expiry_date (max 365 days).
  - Automation: PR -> CI checks -> Security review required for roles granting write to PII-high buckets.

2. Attestation and periodic review:
  - Every role with access to PII-high or audit-buckets must be attested quarterly by the owner.
  - Platform triggers attestation emails and collects attestations in the entitlement audit table.

3. Revocation and emergency rollback:
  - Emergency revoke: security-runbook trigger calls authz-service revoke endpoint and creates an incident.
  - Revert flow: roll back role manifest in infra/authz-roles and apply via infra pipeline.

Least Privilege and Just-in-time Access:
- Default: deny. Temporary elevated access must be timeboxed (max 72 hours) and approved via ticketing system with audit link.
- JIT access issuance recorded as an audit event with requester, approver, TTL, and justification.

Audit Logging Requirements:
- Minimum events to capture:
  - AuthN/AuthZ events (okta login success/failure, token issuance, role assignment).
  - Data access events for PII-high and evidence-bucket reads/writes (who, what, where, why, resource-id, request-id).
  - Admin actions (key rotation, retention changes, policy updates).
  - Evidence creation/export events.

- Log format and schema:
  - Structured JSON: {timestamp, service, env, event_type, principal_id, principal_role, resource_id, action, outcome, request_id, trace_id, metadata} (store as newline-delimited JSON).
  - Example: {"timestamp":"2026-01-12T14:52:03Z","service":"authz-service","event_type":"role.assign","principal_id":"svc-ingest","principal_role":"infra-deployer","resource_id":"bucket:customer-123-evidence","action":"assign","outcome":"success","request_id":"r-abc123"}

- Retention defaults (see retention enforcement section for automation):
  - AuthN/AuthZ events: 2 years (region-specific where required).
  - PII access logs: 7 years or customer contractual minimum (whichever is greater).
  - System telemetry: 90 days aggregated, 365 days indexed metadata.

Audit Pipeline and Evidence Artifacts:
- Ingestion: fluentd -> audit-pipeline (Kafka-backed) -> evidence-bucket (WORM-enabled).
- Evidence artifact composition:
  - Core logs (time-bound sampling window), Role snapshots, KMS key versions, policy documents, and attestations.
  - Artifact metadata: collection_window, collector_version, chain_of_custody_id, digest (SHA256).
- Packaging command (example):
  - ./evidence-orchestrator collect --start 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z --end 2026-01-07T00:00:00Z --tags "customer:acme,incident:INC-1234" --output /tmp/INC-1234-artifact.tar.gz
- Artifact verification: verify digest and store in evidence-index (persistent index with ACLs).

Data Residency and Cross-border Transfers:
- Default behaviour: store customer-specific PII-high data in customer-designated region only. Migration requires legal-approved Data Transfer Agreement and documented justification.
- Authorized flows: replication for DR only, with encryption-in-transit + at-rest and access restricted to DR-owner roles.
- If a customer requests cross-border processing, product must produce a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and a region-specific control matrix.

Retention enforcement (automation):
- Retention rules are codified in infra/retention-policies repo. Each rule has: resource_selector, retention_days, legal_hold_flag, owner.
- Enforcement pipeline periodically (daily) scans evidence-bucket and applies lifecycle policy via cloud API.
- Legal hold overrides: legal_hold_flag must be set by Security or Legal; automated job suspends deletion until release.
- CLI example to set a legal hold (AWS S3):
  - aws s3api put-object-legal-hold --bucket evidence-bucket --key "INC-1234-artifact.tar.gz" --legal-hold Status=ON --region us-west-2

Secure SDLC Integration Points:
- Gate 1 (pre-merge): roles-as-code PRs must pass a policy check (conftest + OPA) to ensure no direct PII-high access without justification.
- Gate 2 (build): build provenance captured and signed with build signer key (KMS). Artifact metadata stored in binary-repo with immutability enabled.
- Gate 3 (deploy): runtime feature flags for data-shielding enabled by default; any opt-outs require security review and elevated approval.

Incident Response and Evidence Preservation:
- Initial triage (0–30 min): classify incident (data exposure vs service disruption). If data exposure suspected, trigger evidence-preserve workflow.
- Evidence preserve workflow steps:
  1. Record incident metadata (INC id, classification, impacted resources, initial reporter).
  2. Call evidence-orchestrator collect with tight window around suspected exposure and write artifact to evidence-bucket with legal_hold ON.
  3. Snapshot role and policy states (authz-service export), KMS key versions, S3 object versions, and runtime cache dumps.
  4. Assign chain_of_custody_id and email chain_of_custody link to Legal and Security.
- Chain of custody requirements: every evidence artifact must record collector identity, collection command, checksum, and signed timestamp. Tampering triggers re-collection if possible.

Compliance Evidence Workflow (audit readiness):
- Quarterly internal readiness run (owner: Security) that exercises an evidence request for a synthetic customer (timebox: 4 hours). Objectives: create artifact, verify digest, produce export, and validate access controls.
- Audit request flow (external):
  1. Security intake validates scope and obtains legal authorization.
  2. Run evidence-orchestrator with reviewer-set tags and store artifact in restricted evidence-bucket.
  3. Produce audit deliverable (README, manifest.json, signed-digest.txt) and deliver via secure transfer (SFTP with expiring token) or dedicated customer SLA channel.

Risk & Exceptions Framework:
- Exceptions allowed only when compensating controls mitigate risk to an acceptable level. Typical compensating controls: additional monitoring, shorter TTL for elevated roles, increased attestation frequency, and enhanced logging sampling.
- Exception request template (required fields): requester, affected_resources, business_justification, duration, compensating_controls, owner, risk_assessment_summary.
- Approval workflow: Security review -> CTO approval for risk score > 7 -> Legal sign-off for cross-border exceptions. All exceptions recorded in exceptions register with automatic expiry.

Operational SLOs and Monitoring:
- Audit-pipeline availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Evidence artifact creation SLA on incident: artifact collected and legal_hold applied within 45 minutes of incident classification.
- Role attestation completion: 95% completion within 14 days of quarterly request. Failure triggers a remediation ticket.

Appendices:
A. Example role manifest (YAML):
---
role_name: analytics-PII-reader
owner: analytics-team
resources:
  - bucket:customer-*-pii
permissions:
  - read
expiry_date: 2026-06-01
justification: "Adhoc analysis for Q2 churn model"

B. Evidence manifest example (manifest.json):
{
  "artifact_id":"INC-2026-0001",
  "collection_window":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z/2026-01-01T02:00:00Z",
  "components":["authz-logs","s3-object-versions","kms-versions","attestations"],
  "digest":"sha256:abcd...",
  "collector":"evidence-orchestrator v1.4.2"
}

C. Frequently used commands and helpers:
- Collect evidence: ./evidence-orchestrator collect --start <start> --end <end> --tags "incident:<id>" --output <path>
- Revoke role (emergency): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://authz.redwood.internal/v1/roles/revoke -d '{"role":"analytics-PII-reader","reason":"compromise"}'

References and related pages:
- infra/authz-roles repo (internal)

Questions or updates:
- For questions, contact the Security team (security@redwood.ai). To propose a change to this playbook, open a PR in security/playbooks and request review from the Security owners listed above.
